Subject: Storage partner runway & risk register — integration handshake

Hi Ari, Marta —

Thanks again for the productive sync last week. We sketched a basic integration runway on the call and I promised to capture the top risks and an operational checklist so both sides can validate go/no-go gates. Attaching an initial risk register and a short integration cookbook (see attachments).

Top asks from Redwood to VectorHub/Pinecone before we enable trial traffic:
- Confirm S3-compatible signed URL policy for cold tier spillover (TTL, pattern)
- Confirm auth method for pgvector write path (service account vs token-per-tenant)
- Ops contacts and escalation matrix for index corruption / re-ingest

We'd like to run a 2-week integration pilot starting Dec 13. Proposed milestones:
1) Week 0 (Dec 6–10): credential exchange, test index creation (dev namespace)
2) Week 1 (Dec 13–17): controlled read/write traffic with synthetic traces, monitoring hooks
3) Week 2 (Dec 20–24): soak testing at 5–10 qps, cold-tier spillover exercise

Can you confirm the milestone dates or suggest adjustments? If we get a nod today we can schedule the kickoff and share invites.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Bennett

From: Ari Shah <ari@pinecone.io>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Storage partner runway & risk register — integration handshake

Laura —

Thanks for the concise plan and the attachments. Reviewed quickly with our eng-ops team; high level feedback below and we'll follow with a short tech-note tomorrow:

- S3 spillover: we support S3 PutObject signed URLs with configurable TTLs. Default TTL is 1h; we can extend to 12h for the pilot. Need an expected object count/size to validate cost and lifecycle.
- pgvector writes: recommend service-account flow for the pilot (easier for scoped access). We'll provide a short script to rotate keys weekly if you want automated rotation.
- Escalation: added our on-call rotations to the shared doc (link in thread). Primary is eng-ops@vectorhub.io.

We can meet on Monday Dec 6 to exchange credentials and run the dev index create. Dec 13 start looks good from our side.

One risk to call out: index version skew between our managed engine and your runtime may cause subtle embedding drift. Suggest we pin the index schema and run a 500-sample similarity regression during Week 1.

I'll follow up with a small tech-note and a couple of curl examples for the signed-url flow.

—Ari
Ari Shah
Developer Relations, Pinecone
ari@pinecone.io

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Storage partner runway & risk register — integration handshake

Team / Ari / Marta —

Attached is a first-draft runbook excerpt (see integration-cookbook-v1.md) for the spillover and reingest flow. Summary of the operational steps we will run in Week 2:

1) Trigger controlled spill: send write traffic with ttl markers to fill the hot index to 80% capacity, verify spill to S3 path redwood/pilots/vectorhub/20261220
2) Confirm signed URLs are created and resolvable by our reingest worker; validate object counts and sizes against expected manifest
3) Run integrity check: compute sha256 on S3 objects and compare with the manifest we keep in the index metadata.
4) Reingest path: rehydrate back into dev-index-2026-12-20 using the same embedding model; run 500-sample similarity regression and compare PR-AUC against baseline (target delta < 1.5%)
5) Rollback: if PR-AUC delta > 1.5% or integrity mismatch, mark pilot as paused and initiate rollback to pre-spill snapshot (snapshot id included in runbook)

Rishi — can you and eng-ops confirm the snapshot retention window and whether we need a snapshot export to partner side for debugging? Ari / Marta — please confirm you can accept signed URLs from the redwood bucket and that TTL extension to 12h is acceptable.

If we get confirmation today, I'll lock invites for Dec 6 kickoff.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
